name: the Parc d'Egmont
title: Ancient Trees in the Parc d'Egmont, Brussels: 6 Giants
meta_description: Where Brussels began its scientific inventory of remarkable trees. Six of them stand in this small park behind the Avenue Louise, including a Turner's oak.
intro: Brussels started its official inventory of remarkable trees in this park, with a squat evergreen oak that most people walk past. The Parc d'Egmont is small, hidden behind the shops of the Avenue Louise, and holds six of the trees we map within a couple of minutes of each other, which makes it one of the densest pockets on the site. Among them is a ginkgo that is the seventh thickest recorded anywhere in the region and is being slowly damaged by the people who like it, and a tulip tree formally adopted by an art institute a few streets away.
